source_refs.note: Book p. 285: 14.4.3 volume of the tetrahedron ABCD = (1/6)[u v w], derivation, figure, Note (ignore negative sign). Book errors: 'place' for plane; middle line 1/3 for 1/6. Teaching notes, Key points, mistakes are ours.

blocks.alt: Tetrahedron ABCD drawn as a diamond with A on the left, C on the right, D at the top and B at the bottom. From A the vectors u along AB, v along AC (cyan) and w along AD are drawn. The base triangle ABC is hatched, and a dashed line drops from D down through the base.
blocks.caption: Figure: tetrahedron ABCD with u = AB, v = AC, w = AD on the hatched base ABC (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: A tetrahedron is a solid with four triangular faces, four vertices and six edges: a pyramid whose base is a triangle. Here the three edges from the vertex \(A\) are the vectors \(\underline{u} = \underline{AB}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{AC}\) and \(\underline{w} = \underline{AD}\), and the triangle \(ABC\) is taken as the base.
Volume of the tetrahedron \(ABCD = \frac{1}{3}\) (area of \(\Delta ABC\))(height of \(D\) above the place \(ABC\))

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints "height of D above the place ABC". It should read "above the plane ABC".

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Two facts are used here. (1) The volume of any pyramid is \(\frac{1}{3}\times\) area of base \(\times\) height (you met this in earlier classes: three equal pyramids fill a prism with the same base and height). (2) The triangle \(ABC\) is half of the parallelogram with sides \(AB\) and \(AC\), and that parallelogram has area \(|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\) (14.3). So area of \(\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2}|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\).
\(= \frac{1}{6}\) (Area of parallelogram with \(AB\) and \(AC\) as adjacent sides) \((h)\)
\(= \frac{1}{3}\) (Volume of the parallelepiped with \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) as edges)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints \(\frac{1}{3}\) in this line. It should be \(\frac{1}{6}\): the parallelogram area times \(h\) is the volume of the parallelepiped (14.4.2), so the line reads \(= \frac{1}{6}\) (Volume of the parallelepiped with \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) as edges), which agrees with the result below.

blocks.text_alt: Volume equals one sixth of (u cross v) dot w, which is one sixth of the box product u v w

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: As volume is always positive, so ignore negative sign if \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w}\) is negative.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
So a tetrahedron takes exactly one sixth of the parallelepiped built on the same three edges. In practice, for a tetrahedron with vertices \(A, B, C, D\):
\[V = \dfrac{1}{6}\left|[\underline{AB}\ \underline{AC}\ \underline{AD}]\right|\]
All three vectors must start from the same vertex. Any vertex can be chosen; the answer is the same. Example 26 uses this formula.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Quick check with a corner of a box: \(O(0,0,0)\), \(A(1,0,0)\), \(B(0,2,0)\), \(C(0,0,3)\). The edges from \(O\) are \(\underline{i}, 2\underline{j}, 3\underline{k}\) and \([\underline{i}\ \ 2\underline{j}\ \ 3\underline{k}] = 6\), so \(V = \frac{1}{6}(6) = 1\). Directly: the base \(OAB\) is a right triangle of area \(\frac{1}{2}(1)(2) = 1\), the height is \(3\), and \(\frac{1}{3}(1)(3) = 1\). Same answer.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Volume of a tetrahedron \(= \frac{1}{3}\) (area of base)(height).
2. Area of \(\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2}|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\).
3. Volume \(= \frac{1}{6}[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}]\): one sixth of the parallelepiped on the same edges.
4. If the triple product is negative, ignore the sign: volume is positive.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Using \(\frac{1}{3}\) (as the book's misprinted line does) or \(\frac{1}{2}\) instead of \(\frac{1}{6}\).
2. Taking vectors that do not start from one vertex, e.g. \(\underline{AB}\), \(\underline{BC}\), \(\underline{CD}\) mixed carelessly; use \(\underline{AB}, \underline{AC}, \underline{AD}\).
3. Writing a negative volume.
